narrative.h2: Narrative MVs are mini-films, and the rules of film apply

sections.heading: What narrative MV requires
sections.body: Narrative music video tells a story across the song's duration - characters with at least one arc, a setting that means something, beats that pay off by the bridge or outro. The format treats the song as the score and the visual as a 3-4 minute short film. The discipline borrowed from film: a clear premise in the first 15 seconds, a turn around the halfway point, an image at the end that recontextualizes what came before. Music videos that win at this read like trailers for a movie that doesn't exist.

sections.heading: When to use it
sections.body: Narrative MV is the right call for songs that already tell a story (Bruce Springsteen, country, story-rap), for album-cycle anchor singles where budget concentrates on one statement piece, for artists building a cinematic brand (Childish Gambino's This Is America, Lana Del Rey's Ride, anything Hiro Murai directs). It's also the format awards take seriously - the VMA for Video of the Year skews narrative. The trade-off is cost and time, both of which Tunee compresses dramatically.

sections.heading: Tunee prompting tip
sections.body: Structure the prompt by song section, not by shot: 'verse 1: protagonist alone in apartment, morning light, slow handheld; pre-chorus: leaves the building, color shifts cooler; chorus: wide-shot on empty highway, golden hour'. Tunee can interpret song-section prompting. Reference one director for unified language: 'Hiro Murai for the whole video' beats mixed reference per section. Plan the final image first and work backward - narrative MV is judged on the ending.
